1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).

   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.
3. Reply with exactly three lines and nothing else:
   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.
4. On "yes" / "open": in a local session run `open <path>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <path>` (Linux) and confirm in one line; in a session with an artifact/publish tool, publish the HTML and give the link instead. On "no", stop.
5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).
2. Run `python3 ~/.ops-agents/scripts/render-brief.py <that file>` → the `.html` beside it.

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.

1. Write the merged result as JSON to `~/.ops-agents/briefs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.json` following `~/.ops-agents/templates/brief.schema.md` (blind spots in `not_checked`, never in `items`; the full shared output block goes in the JSON `capabilities`/`items`, not in chat).

   `<one headline sentence, including the count of needs-you items and the count of sources not checked>`
   `Brief: <absolute path to the .html>`
   `Open it? (yes)`
   No item list, no capabilities, no output block in chat — the page carries all of it.

5. Only after the operator opens or declines the page, answer follow-up questions from the JSON; `TRACK?` items are listed on the page and acted on only when the operator says "track".
For single-domain questions (one specialist), skip the page: reply in text with the shared output block.
